title: Written orders, prior authorization and program activation: Urology and Continence Supply Program
content:
Every shipment on the Urology and Continence Supply Program rests on a written order from the treating prescriber. The order names the item, the billing units per 30 days, the order date and the prescriber's NPI.

## Written orders

- The order is valid for the tier's order validity, in calendar months counted from its order date. The valid-through date is the day before the same calendar day that many months later, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist. Larkfield records that valid-through date when the order is received.
- A prior authorization request and an authorization grant each rest on a written order on file for the item. The order is identified by its own record, and that record is the one the request or the grant is based on.

**Hypothetical order:** an order dated 10 April on a tier with 12 months' validity is valid through 9 April of the following year.

## Authorization by tier type

| Tier type | How the authorization grant arises | Span of the grant |
|---|---|---|
| Prior authorization required | Once the written order is on file, Larkfield submits a prior authorization request to the payer, and the program moves from referral received to pending authorization. The payer's approval is recorded as a grant on the basis of the payer's prior authorization, carrying the payer's PA reference, the approved units and the approved span. | The tier's authorization validity in calendar months from the decision date. If the payer's approval states an earlier valid-through date, the payer's date governs. |
| No prior authorization | Larkfield records the grant itself on the basis of the written order. On the self-pay tier the basis is the self-pay order. | From the order date through the order's valid-through date, for the billing units the order covers within that span. |

## Request priority and payer decision time

A prior authorization request is submitted as expedited only when the prescriber states on the order that waiting the standard decision time could seriously jeopardize the patient's life or health. Otherwise it is standard. The payer is expected to decide within the tier's standard decision time in calendar days of a standard request, or within the tier's expedited decision time in hours of an expedited one.

## Renewal of a prior authorization

A renewal request for a prior authorization may be submitted no earlier than the tier's renewal lead, in calendar days, before the valid-through date of the authorization it renews. The lead is counted backward in calendar days from that valid-through date, and submission on the earliest day itself is allowed. The renewal also requires a written order that is valid beyond that valid-through date.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, 30-day renewal lead, authorization valid through day 100):**

| Submission day | Permitted? |
|---|---|
| day 69 | no: it is earlier than 30 days before the valid-through date |
| day 70 | yes: it is the earliest permitted day |
| day 85 | yes |

## Activation

A program is activated only when an authorization grant on file for the program is valid on the activation date. On a prior-authorization tier, the program becomes active when the payer's approval is recorded as a grant. On other tiers it becomes active when the written order is on file and its order-based grant is recorded.

## Denials and clinical documents

- A payer denial of a prior authorization is recorded with the payer's denial reason. The program stays in pending authorization while the prescriber supplies further documentation or a new request is made. It closes only under the hold and closure rules.
- Clinical documents are recorded with the purpose they serve and the visit date they document. A document serves only the purpose recorded on it.
